correctness.rationale: For every n>=3, a binary edge coloring is equivalent to three explicit two-of-four neighbor equations at each top, bottom and rung edge. One rung equation forces rail sums to all one (alternating zero/two gives an immediate binary contradiction); subtraction then enforces period-four top and opposite bottom colours; rung colors alternate. This gives necessary 4|n and exactly 4*2=8 labeled solutions, and each construction checks back into the sufficient equations. The even 2n Hamiltonian cycle with leftover perfect matching gives a proper three-edge coloring on every cubic prism and hence a strong majority edge coloring. A separate verifier builds and checks actual edge-incidence neighbor lists, exhausts binary n=3..7, and checks Hamiltonian and eight constructions n=3..44. Direct finite checks do not replace proof.
